roofIndependentAudit.text:
CLEAN — the two completed d356290 roof controls have consistent native PASS evidence. This audit covers only `prepared_air_recovery_bucket` on exact Minecraft 1.21.1 and 26.3, using frozen source commit `d356290185ebda5b504f036f457ba58e5938a9c8`. I read both complete raw receipts, runner records, class-source provenance, artifact metadata and bounded AIR/craft log sequences. No material discrepancy found.

The fixture is disclosed: an isolated superflat integrated server supplies three iron ingots, two cooked beef, health three, food twenty with zero saturation, initial air 200, fifty source-water cells, a bedrock-bounded 5×5 pool, twenty-four roof blocks with one exit gap, a supported dry ledge and a crafting table. These are prepared control runs, not natural-world acquisition evidence.

Both runs actually rose through the roof gap, landed on the supported ledge, refilled air and then crafted the requested bucket. The new arrival hold appears twice in each log: at waypoint `(2,65,0)` with actual feet Y64.7335008437787, and at `(2,66,0)` with feet Y65.81348296777863. Primary log lines 138–139 and modern lines 304–306 show these decisions on attempt one. Modern line 307 also records the held rising column: X2.699999988079071, upward velocity, zero intended/applied horizontal input and jump held while below Y66. Primary line 141 observes the following ledge step only after feet reach Y66.1096291306. These are arrival-decision diagnostics; they do not independently certify every collision observation.

Primary lines 142–143 and modern lines 309–311 show supported breathing/refill followed by completion on attempt one, after 3,051ms and 3,120ms respectively. Both routes contain five swim waypoints; there is no route retry or native-path launch in these AIR sequences. Modern line 310 directly records `onGround=true`, dry head, no water contact, released movement input and `KeyboardInput`. Primary support is corroborated by the breathing transition, unchanged fixture ledge and integrated-server position samples. In both runs the server settles at `(3.012680131685625,66.0,0.5)` and stays there through the remaining receipt samples.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial observed air | 169/300 | 177/300 |
| Minimum monitored air | 138/300 | 145/300 |

Causal ordering is supported by independent server observations and ordinary production logs. At the AIR transition, crafting-table openings are zero; at AIR completion, bucket count is zero, head is dry and air is already at least 270. The later logs show eating, health recovery, the bucket CRAFT step, complete station contents and task completion: primary lines 145–153; modern lines 312–326. Final server inventory is exactly one bucket and one cooked beef, with no iron remaining. Thus three supplied iron became one bucket, and one supplied cooked beef was consumed. Exactly one table opening, no furnace opening, empty initial/final cursor, unchanged empty equipment maps, stopped navigation and idle foreground/maintenance queues are recorded. These roof receipts do not separately establish exact original input-object identity, all native settings or selected-slot restoration.

The runner binds each run to the frozen artifact and reports unchanged artifact bytes, clean source at launch, exit code zero, no timeout/failures and a passed native receipt gate. I physically rehashed both jars, both raw receipts, runners and logs. The complete launch classpaths remove development production outputs and retain the isolated verifier outputs. Class-load evidence places primary production in Fabric's freshly remapped frozen jar and modern production directly in its frozen jar; the native verifier loads from its separate verification output. Source audits report 387 primary and 397 modern production classes, zero foreign-kernel classes and zero violations. The primary runtime-remap audit preserves all 145 core and 40 navigation class bytes and maps the loaded production classes to the input/output artifacts.

All 75 primary and 65 modern frozen verification-output files physically match `verification-outputs.json`; there are no missing or extra files in the recorded output directories. Later cooking source drafts therefore do not substitute for these compiled verifier bytes. The artifact manifest's `nativeStatus=unrun` is its pre-run freeze status, not a verdict on these completed receipts.

limits: Prepared fixture and unchanged assertions/deadlines; no natural gameplay or user acceptance claim.
Both roof controls witness two new height holds, first-route supported ledge landing and refill before real bucket crafting. This does not certify every native-path entity or descending edge.
Both pending-attack controls retain one unknown native send through escape and real stop, with no resend/output credit and restored input/settings/selection/cursor.

Primary pending-transfer fails after an explicitly logged live observation slice expiry at the second height hold. The current-step proof has at most eleven work observations, below its 128 cap, so this yield is wall-clock expiry; exact logger duration is not measured.

Later replanning begins at feet Y66.092 with original episode minimum Y65. Its final refused body minimum Y64.857 is outside that vertical domain; sampled horizontal drift remains within the original limits.

The sheep health-decrease counter effects=1 does not count attack sends. The final health8-to6 observation at submersion+320 server ticks fits native drowning; its exact damage source and final actor send count are absent, so exclusive causal attribution is unproved.

Frozen source keeps the shear actor in DRAIN and paused ticks return before dispatch. Borrowed shears remain a restoration debt; no real stop was issued because the verifier waits for successful AIR completion. Tool return and refill are unproved in this failed run.
Cooking drafts were restored only after both roof controls and after freezing the production artifact and verifier outputs. They were not compiled into the animal-run artifacts.
Modern transfer remains unrun after the primary failure. Earlier animal passes remain evidence of their earlier exact artifacts.
The broader LIVE timeout-to-route-cancellation behavior remains unchanged in the subsequent logger-timing-only unit; typed yielding without stale movement is a separate design seam.

transferIndependentDiagnoses.text:
# d356290 primary AIR-transfer pause diagnosis A

**No post-pause animal attack send is established by this receipt.** The witnessed AIR route fails and pauses. The later zero-damage preservation check fails when the submerged fixture sheep loses two health. Its timing matches native drowning. The frozen engine/actor interlock prevents normal animal effect dispatch during pause and preserves the borrowed shears debt. Do not change that interlock to fix a damage-counter interpretation.

This is read-only diagnosis of commit `d356290185ebda5b504f036f457ba58e5938a9c8` in `/Users/luinbytes/src/lodekeeper`. All source reads used that explicit committed object, including both Engines and PlayerActions; uncompiled cooking drafts were excluded. No source/Git writes, builds, tests, clients, restarts or nested agents. Actual actor files are `AnimalHarvestAction.java` in the two adapter families.

## Chronological raw facts

Authority is `/tmp/lodekeeper-native-animal-d356290-air_pending_transfer-primary-r1/run/verification/evidence/run-2026-10-09T03-27-20-323997Z-73a38914.json` and its `run/logs/latest.log`.

1. Client tick234 observes the real main20 PICKUP with selected hotbar1, shears cursor, job1/one exact sheep UUID, and **zero actor sends**. The disclosed server pool is installed at server tick115. Initially that sheep has eight health; original shears are ordinary, wear0, main20; selected0 and cursor empty.
2. Client tick242 observes the AIR route. Its server tick123 receipt has selected1, source20 absent, staging1 occupied and cursor empty. `pendingEvidenceAtAirRoute=false`: the original transfer has settled before the moving route observation. This case does not witness an unknown click remaining unresolved throughout swimming.
3. Log139 starts the seven-step swim at 203 ms, attempt1. Log144/147 record the new height holds. Log148 reports a LIVE observation slice expiry; log149 releases/retries at Y65.8251296. Retained native planning then reanchors five times (151–155).
4. Log156 refuses at actual Y64.8573262 because retained planning leaves the original domain; log157 pauses at 04:27:41 local time. Root owns that movement-domain/deadline diagnosis separately. This report neither proposes loosening that proof nor treats the AIR failure as successful cancellation/restoration.
5. Log160 and164 still show the same **paused** engine at server ticks261 and360, same job/stock/player position. The verifier does not yet report a send/identity violation. It finally fails at server tick435 (log166).
6. Final raw server receipt: sheep8→6, `effects=1`, sheared0, dead0, ordinaryBeef0, source20 absent, staging1 occupied, selected1, cursor empty, player air−10 and head submerged. Player health is20 in the PEACEFUL fixture. The requested wool is0. There is no final actor-send count or native damage-source/attack-packet observation in this JSON.

## Why effects=1 is not attacks=1

Frozen primary `fabric-1211/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/VerificationApi.java:125–128` increments `fixture.effects` whenever sampled animal health decreases. Modern `fabric-modern/src/verification/java/dev/lodekeeper/fabric/modern/VerificationApi.java:125–128` does the same. Neither records a packet, attacker, attack invocation or damage source. RuntimeVerification's generic failure OR includes this zero-health-loss condition at primary1985–2021, particularly2018, separately from `action.sentEffects` at2015.

The fixture leaves its adult NoAI sheep in water (same helper101–119); only the player is teleported and given air170. The sheep's initial ordinary air budget is300. Server435−submersion115 is exactly320 ticks. The cached exact1.21.1 `LivingEntity.baseTick` bytecode decrements submerged air (offsets311–320), checks−20 (323–329), resets it and applies `DamageSources.drown()` with2 damage (464–473). That explains the precise late8→6 preservation failure without requiring an attack send.

Drowning is the strong source/timing-supported attribution; the retained raw receipt lacks the damage source, so it cannot prove exclusivity. Calling the row an animal attack would overstate the evidence. Final `shearsDamage=-1` also means the helper found no shears in **source20**; it is not observed wear of the borrowed tool in hotbar1.

## Frozen production flow in both mirrors

**AIR handoff is drain-only.** Primary AnimalHarvestAction110–121 and modern116–127 set `drainRequested=true; phase=DRAIN` before handing movement to AIR.
